content.title: Wayne Player remains banned from Augusta ahead of Masters
content.text: Augusta National still enforcing Wayne Player ban Wayne Player will not attend the 90th Masters to watch his father, Gary Player, open the tournament, as he remains barred from Augusta National. The ban followed a 2021 incident during the Honorary Starters ceremony honoring Lee Elder, when Wayne held a box of OnCore golf balls in view of cameras. That act led officials to revoke his badge and extend the penalty indefinitely. Sports Illustrated + 1 The 2021 stunt that led to the ban During a moment meant to celebrate Lee Elder's historic role at the Masters, Wayne Player stood nearby holding a branded golf ball box, which was widely perceived as a marketing stunt. Wayne later admitted it was a 'tacky thing' and said it was not premeditated. Augusta National dealt with the matter quietly, without a formal public announcement. The Spun Wayne Player's apology and Gary Player's response Wayne Player attempted to regain entry to Augusta National by sending an apology letter, but his request was declined. Gary Player publicly supported the club's decision, saying that if someone does something wrong, 'you don’t want him back here again, then just bar him.' This stance highlights Gary’s respect for the Masters' traditions even in a personal matter. Sports Illustrated + 1 Why the ban resonates during Masters week Wayne Player’s continued absence during a landmark Masters illustrates Augusta National’s strict approach to preserving its image and traditions. The club’s decisive handling of the matter aligns with past actions to protect the tournament’s integrity, including prompt responses to on-course issues and patron misconduct. This consistency reinforces the cultural and ceremonial standards that define the Masters experience. Golf + 2 3 references
